free_tier.stated: Custom TCP/UDP applications require an Enterprise plan with Spectrum as a paid add-on.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published. The plan table gives 'TCP' and 'UDP' as 'Paid add-on' on Enterprise and 'No' on Free, Pro and Business; Enterprise Spectrum is metered per GB at an unpublished rate.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: configured through the Cloudflare dashboard or the API; Spectrum applications are created per protocol and port
tooling: Cloudflare dashboard or API; no client-side daemon
chaining: composes with any free VM as the origin: the VM keeps its own address private and the anycast address is the published one, which is what a WireGuard or game endpoint needs.

limits.value: custom TCP/UDP needs an Enterprise plan with Spectrum as a paid add-on

binding_note: No byte count fails at 1 TiB/month; the Enterprise contract is the gate. The only sub-Enterprise route is a Pro or Business plan, where Spectrum is limited to a single Minecraft app (UDP for Bedrock) and a single SSH app.

identity_cost.detail: An Enterprise contract with Cloudflare sales, plus a domain on Cloudflare. The Pro and Business plans carry Spectrum only for 'Minecraft (one app allowed)' and 'SSH (one app allowed)'.

confidence_note: The support matrix and the Enterprise requirement are on the pages read today. The per-GB rate and the Pro add-on price are not published, so the cost side stays unverified.

evidence.proved: Spectrum provides security and acceleration for any TCP or UDP based application, and custom TCP/UDP applications require an Enterprise plan with Spectrum as a paid add-on
Availability: No on Free, Paid add-on on Enterprise; TCP and UDP are No on Pro and Business; Minecraft (one app allowed) and SSH (one app allowed) are Yes on Pro and Business

notes: The benchmark. Cloudflare Magic Transit is the adjacent product and is not a substitute: it takes a /24 and BGP or GRE from the customer, where Spectrum takes an origin IP and a port. Two things stay open: the Enterprise per-GB rate, and whether the Pro-tier Minecraft slot is usable for a Bedrock (UDP) server rather than only Java (TCP) - the table names the game, not the protocol.

extras.wg_detail: Spectrum forwards arbitrary UDP to an origin port, so a WireGuard listener on the origin is reachable through the anycast address; no .conf is issued.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published. The plan table gives 'TCP' and 'UDP' as 'Paid add-on' on Enterprise and 'No' on Free, Pro and Business; Enterprise Spectrum is metered per GB at an unpublished rate.
extras.transit_note: Cloudflare carries the bytes between its edge and the origin
